hints: Start by writing the balanced equation for the complete combustion of methane in oxygen, and notice what the products are.
Recall the Hess cycle rule that reaction enthalpy equals the sum of formation enthalpies of products minus the sum for reactants.
Apply that rule to your balanced equation, remembering that oxygen as an element in its standard state contributes nothing to the sum.
walkthrough:
**Write the balanced combustion equation**

Think of combustion simply as burning in oxygen to make carbon dioxide and water. For methane this needs balancing carefully.

Chemical equation or calculation rule if applicable:
$$\text{CH}_4 + 2\text{O}_2 \rightarrow \text{CO}_2 + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}$$

**Apply the Hess law formation rule**

Hess law lets us find any reaction enthalpy from formation data. The friendly rule is products minus reactants.

Chemical equation or calculation rule if applicable:
$$\Delta H_r^\ominus = \sum \Delta H_f^\ominus(\text{products}) - \sum \Delta H_f^\ominus(\text{reactants})$$

**Substitute for methane combustion**

Products are 1 mole of $\text{CO}_2$ and 2 moles of $\text{H}_2\text{O}$. Reactants are 1 mole of $\text{CH}_4$ and 2 moles of $\text{O}_2$.

Chemical equation or calculation rule if applicable:
$$\Delta H_c^\ominus = [\Delta H_f^\ominus(\text{CO}_2) + 2\Delta H_f^\ominus(\text{H}_2\text{O})] - [\Delta H_f^\ominus(\text{CH}_4) + 2\Delta H_f^\ominus(\text{O}_2)]$$

**Simplify using the element rule**

Oxygen is an element in its standard state, so its standard enthalpy of formation is zero. It drops out of the expression.

Chemical equation or calculation rule if applicable:
$$\Delta H_c^\ominus = \Delta H_f^\ominus(\text{CO}_2) + 2\Delta H_f^\ominus(\text{H}_2\text{O}) - \Delta H_f^\ominus(\text{CH}_4)$$

options.A: Incorrect. This adds the reactant $\text{CH}_4$ to a product and subtracts water, which reverses the products minus reactants logic. It treats $\text{CH}_4$ as if it were a product and $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ as if it were a reactant.
options.B: Incorrect. This adds all formation enthalpies together. The common trap is forgetting the minus sign for reactants, so $\Delta H_f^\ominus(\text{CH}_4)$ is added instead of subtracted.
options.C: Incorrect. This is the reverse of the correct expression, with reactants minus products. It gives the negative of the combustion enthalpy and swaps the roles of $\text{CO}_2$ and $\text{CH}_4$.
options.D: Correct. Products ($\text{CO}_2 + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}$) minus reactants ($\text{CH}_4$, since $\text{O}_2$ is zero) gives exactly this expression. This matches the balanced equation $\text{CH}_4 + 2\text{O}_2 \rightarrow \text{CO}_2 + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}$.
